claims.text: Pre-aging FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings in an oxidative environment promotes formation of a Cr/Cu-rich protective oxide layer.
The pre-aging-induced Cr/Cu-rich oxide layer is self-healing.
The Cr/Cu-rich oxide layer governs the high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
Pre-aging enhances the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings under high-temperature mechanical loading.
The baseline as-deposited coating has a uniform composition and limited pre-existing oxide formation.
The intervention is thermal pre-aging in an oxygen-containing atmosphere at 400–600°C before wear testing.
Thermal pre-aging selectively oxidizes Cr and Cu.
The oxide formed by pre-aging is self-limiting.
The protective oxide acts as a barrier that reduces direct metal-to-metal contact.
Reduced direct metal-to-metal contact lowers wear and improves high-temperature tribological performance.
Pre-aged coatings will have lower high-temperature wear rates than as-deposited coatings.
Pre-aged coatings will have lower high-temperature friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings.
Pre-aged coatings will exhibit a continuous and adherent Cr/Cu-rich oxide layer.
As-deposited coatings form less protective or non-optimized oxide layers during high-temperature wear.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to thin FeNiCrCoCu coatings tested at 400–600°C under controlled mechanical loading.

contradictions.description: The conditions field describes comparison against room-temperature baseline wear tests, whereas the baseline, predicted outcome, and falsification experiment compare pre-aged and as-deposited coatings under identical high-temperature wear conditions.
